before: Two participants who split one paragraph at different points at the same time each listed a new paragraph right after it, and Yjs ordered the new paragraphs by client ID. When the paragraph that holds the later tail came first, a moved copy showed in the last paragraph that held it, so the earlier tail showed in the later paragraph, the earlier paragraph showed nothing, and one split looked lost.
after: Paragraphs that a parent lists side by side and that went in concurrently at one place show in the order of the text they copy: the paragraph whose first copied character comes first in the text it was copied from comes first, and when that text is deleted, a paragraph that holds the first character another one copied, after characters of its own, comes first. A paragraph listed later right after one of them, such as a paragraph split off it, moves with it. The materializer, the projection of local edits, and the document order that decides where a moved copy shows read this one rule, so when two participants split one paragraph at different points at the same time, the new paragraphs show in text order, and later edits land where they show. Each replica reads the order once per change of the parent's listing or of a paragraph's text in the run, not once per comparison.
reason: The rule changes which paragraph shows a moved copy for the same shared state, so it is repair semantics: a replica with repairVersion 2 shows other text in other paragraphs for the same state, and local edits on the two would address different paragraphs. repairVersion increases to 3, so a replica refuses a room that another repair version created before it applies any update. A room created with repairVersion 2 keeps the earlier rules, because only replicas with that version edit it. The rule reads only shared state every replica holds alike, independent of garbage collection, and writes nothing, so no stored field or identity changes. Tracked concurrent splits still keep one of the proposed paragraph marks on the split paragraph, so one proposed break has no revision and Reject All leaves it; two splits by each peer in one paragraph, a break at the end with a split in the middle, and a redo after both undos are not settled yet.
